business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Wholesale Trade of Aged Scotch and Bordeaux Wines

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law and French Civil Law heritages under the Constitution of Vanuatu 1980, with statutory recognition of customary law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus)
EU-Pacific States Economic Partnership Agreement (interim regional EPA)

No Vanuatu bilateral investment treaty or comprehensive double taxation agreement with a major OECD economy is currently in force; investment-protection capacity resides in the trade agreements listed above.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 7 of 2020 (as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit Act No. 1 of 2020; AML/CFT Regulations 2020; International Companies Act [Cap. 222], ss. 10-16 (incorporation, name, registered office and registered agent) as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2016 imposing beneficial-ownership record-keeping obligations on registered agents; International Companies Regulations 1993; VFSC Company and Trust Supervision Handbook and AML/CFT Supervisory Circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin or Vanuatu Commissioner of Oaths for local witnessing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Vanuatu is a Contracting Party effective 2 September 2008) or consular legalization if the country of origin is not an Apostille State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility provider or account-holding licensed bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter confirming account conduct and source of wealth
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding licensed bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (at bank protocol requirement)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional reference letter from a licensed lawyer or certified accountant supporting the promoter and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing, incumbency, and UBO register extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or licensed registered agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of all promoters, directors, shareholders (direct and indirect), and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, HM Treasury UK sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic Vanuatu FIU/VFSC designations; continuing screening applies for the life of the relationship. PEPs (foreign, domestic, and international-organisation functionaries) trigger mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence: source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval, increased transaction monitoring, and VFSC reporting per Part 4 (ss. 26-32) of the AML/CFT Act 2020. The bonded wine and spirits wholesale trade under ISIC 4632 is classified Medium_Risk_Enhanced, requiring EDD for counterparties and jurisdictions identified by the FATF or APG, and verification that all bonded-excise and customs documentation matches the names and identities screened at onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — Company Registry Online Name Reservation and Incorporation Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The International Companies Act [Cap. 222] requires the company name to be expressed in Roman/Latin characters; English and French forms are standard and Bislama names are acceptable in Latin script. Names must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Corp', 'Incorporated', 'Inc', 'Société Anonyme', 'SA', or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'/'SARL'. Names in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) are not registrable in the original script and require a uniform romanized transliteration approved by the Registrar; the registered Latin-script name is the exclusive legal name for all instruments, banking, SWIFT references, bills of lading, customs and excise documentation, and bonded transfer records.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or deceptively similar to an existing Vanuatu registered company, a reserved name, or a foreign company registered in Vanuatu
Tokens importing connection with the Government of Vanuatu or State agencies: 'Government', 'National', 'State', 'Municipal', 'Ministry', 'Official', 'Republic'

Restricted financial-sector words requiring prior ministerial or VFSC licensing consent: 'Bank', 'Banker', 'Banking', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Reinsurance', 'Trust', 'Trustee', 'Building Society', 'Fund', 'Deposit', 'Custody', 'Fiduciary', 'Pension', 'Superannuation', 'Broker', 'Clearing'

Words considered misleading as to the business of the company, including 'Wines', 'Spirits', or 'Bonded' tokens where the company does not hold or is not actively applying for the requisite Customs bonded-warehouse or liquor licence
Names that are obscene, contrary to the national interest, or comprising chiefly/title words protected under customary law
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon VFSC rejection, the applicant's licensed registered agent must, within 14 days of the rejection notice, file a written review application addressed to the Registrar of International Companies under s. 11 of the International Companies Act [Cap. 222], stating the legal and factual grounds and proposing mitigating distinguishing elements. The Registrar must issue a determination within 21 days of receipt; silence for 21 days constitutes deemed rejection of the first review. If the decision remains adverse, the applicant may file an originating application for judicial review in the Supreme Court of Vanuatu within 30 days of the deemed or express rejection. If the original reservation lapses at 30 days without incorporation, the registered agent may immediately re-file a fresh reservation application with a new fee; a single 60-day extension is available upon written application to the VFSC and payment of the extension tariff before expiry of the original reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permissible as the statutory registered office: s. 13 of the International Companies Act requires a physical registered office in Vanuatu maintained by a licensed registered agent (TCSP licensee). Remote commercial operations, including remote management of the bonded wine and spirits trade, are permissible provided all registers, instrument files, and books are physically retrievable through the Vanuatu registered office. For the bonded trade specifically, Vanuatu law requires an operational physical bonded warehouse or a formal contracting arrangement with a customs-licensed bonded facility in the importing jurisdiction (e.g., a UK bonded warehouse for Scotch or a French bonded warehouse for Bordeaux); a purely virtual or paper-only presence will disqualify the Customs bonded-warehouse licence and the liquor wholesale licence under the Liquor Licensing Act [Cap. 92].
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk — registered office and corporate records: 'Low to moderate' (approximately 15% per annum) for targeted VFSC documented inspections, rising to 'high' (approximately 60%) where adverse media, regulatory referrals, or APG mutual-evaluation cycles are present. Bonded liquor and wholesale licensed operations: 'elevated' (approximately 40%) risk of unannounced physical stock, stamp/excise, and customs-origin inspections by Vanuatu Customs and the Liquor Licensing Board where the company operates a physical licensed bonded warehouse in Vanuatu. If trading through a third-country bonded facility (Scotch in the UK, Bordeaux in France), inspection risk transfers to the foreign competent authorities, while Vanuatu supervisory agencies retain AML/CFT inspection rights over the registered agent's UBO filings and record-keeping (approximately 20%).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1992, Part II (ss. 3–18) and Part V, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2002; Companies (Name and Consequential Provisions) Regulation 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division, Port Vila, Efate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Application for Registration as an International Company, together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association and the registered agent acceptance form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. At least one share must be subscribed, and shares may be issued with no par value. Consideration may remain unpaid. No escrow account, capital deposit, or capital undertaking is required under Vanuatu law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a meeting of the board of directors duly convened, the following resolutions were adopted unanimously: 1. Resolved that the subscription and exchange of capital be confirmed and that the directors are authorized to issue, allot, and record shares to subscribers under the Memorandum and Articles. 2. Resolved that the registered office be established at the office of the licensed registered agent in Port Vila, Vanuatu. 3. Resolved that [Name] be appointed Managing Director, [Name] Company Secretary, and [Name] Compliance Officer, each authorized to sign documents and open bank accounts. 4. Resolved that the officers execute all filing and licensing applications required for bonded wine and spirits wholesale operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Companies Registry, Name Reservation Unit, Port Vila.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed Name Reservation Form listing up to three preferred names in priority order, either through the VFSC eServices portal or through a licensed registered agent. Pay the reservation fee and obtain a valid name reservation certificate before filing the incorporation application. The reservation is valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: List of proposed company names in priority order
Authorisation letter from licensed registered agent
Identity pages of proposed directors and subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused, file a written objection with the VFSC within seven days or select a different name and resubmit the reservation without a new statutory filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed registered agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles in the exact form required by the International Companies Act 1992. The subscribers execute the constitutional documents, and each director and officer signs consent to act. The registered agent retains the executed originals and the statutory records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VFSC returns a correction notice, the registered agent amends the constitutional documents and re-executes them; resubmission is processed within two working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 with the executed Memorandum and Articles, name reservation certificate, and registered office/agent details. Pay the government incorporation fee. The application must include client due diligence documentation and may be submitted electronically through the VFSC licensed agent channel.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Application for Registration as an International Company
Notice of registered office and registered agent
CDD/KYC package for shareholders and directors
Consent to act from each director and officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VFSC raises a query, respond in writing within ten business days with the requested clarification or corrected document; resubmissions receive priority processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After verification, VFSC issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the certificate for exact company number, registered name, and incorporation date. Retain the certificate in the company minute book and present it to banks and licensing authorities as proof of legal formation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by VFSC
Initial register of members and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical or legal-name errors, file a Notice of Correction with VFSC; a corrected certificate is issued within three business days at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a duly-noticed board meeting or execute a unanimous written consent. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution approving share subscription, adopting the registered office, and appointing officers. Ensure the resolution and minutes are signed and stored at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Notice of board meeting or unanimous written consent
Register of directors, officers, and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board meeting is not quorate, circulate the resolution for unanimous written consent under the Articles; if a director declines consent, appoint an alternate and re-file the statutory register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC, licensed registered agent, and corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the annual government fee for the current year through the registered agent, file the initial beneficial ownership declaration required under the disclosure regime, and open corporate bank accounts. All accounting records and statutory registers must be kept at the registered office or as directed by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Board resolution authorising bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual fee is paid late, pay the prescribed penalty and obtain a receipt; for a rejected bank application, provide updated source-of-funds evidence and resubmit within five business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Department of Customs and Inland Revenue (DCIR), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, for the Bonded Warehouse Licence; Liquor Licensing Board, Ministry of Internal Affairs, for the Liquor Wholesale Off-Licence; and Vanuatu Investment Promotion Authority for the business licence registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Bonded Warehouse Licence under the Customs Act 2013 and Liquor Wholesale Off-Licence under the Liquor Act [Cap 81]

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology, Geo-Hazards, Environment, Energy and Disaster Management
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 – Environmental Registration with an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP); no full EIA is required for enclosed bonded storage and wholesale distribution where no vinification, distillation, or other manufacturing process is present.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from washing and spill clean-ups requires an effluent permit and must not be discharged to water bodies; standards: pH 6.0–8.5, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, TSS ≤ 100 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L. Storage areas must have secondary spill containment of at least 110% of the largest container. Venting and transfer operations must control VOCs to ≤ 20 g/m³ using vapour-recovery and sealed gauging. Waste spirits and contaminated packaging must be removed by a licensed waste contractor under manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance Certificate from Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Services; structural viability and racking-load approval from the Department of Public Works; occupational health and workplace registration under the Employment (Occupational Health and Safety) Act; approval of the emergency response plan, fire suppression system, lighting, ventilation, and storage segregation for spirits and wines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Commission (VCIRC), Ministry of Finance and Treasury, Port Vila; operational contact desks at the VAT and Excise Section; official national portal maintained at gov.vu with no fully automated fiscal e-filing platform as of the current regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first incorporate an International Company under the International Companies Act [Cap 222] through a licensed registered agent and obtain a business licence from the Vanuatu Investment Promotion Authority (VIPA). The IC then applies in writing to the Commissioner of VAT on the prescribed VCIRC registration form, submitting the certificate of incorporation, registered office and agent details, projected 12-month turnover, ownership structure, and bank references. The Commission assigns a unique VAT identification number (also used as the customs client code for import/export clearances). Compulsory registration is triggered once annual taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold; voluntary registration is available below threshold. Processing normally completes within 5 to 15 working days, and the VAT number must appear on all tax invoices and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: a Vanuatu International Company is a non-resident limited liability vehicle classified within the exempt offshore zone. It is outside the Vanuatu income tax base because Vanuatu levies no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no withholding tax. The IC is nevertheless within the territorial scope of the Value Added Tax Act for supplies sourced in or imported into Vanuatu and must zero-rate its offshore bonded-trade exports to non-resident buyers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists because Vanuatu imposes no entity-level income tax. Statutorily available elections include: (i) voluntary VAT registration under the VAT Act for ICs below the compulsory threshold; (ii) election by the IC to abandon exempt international status and operate as an ordinary resident company by obtaining an in-country business licence from VIPA; and (iii) election of the bonded warehouse deferred-entry regime by which customs duty, excise, and VAT are suspended until goods are withdrawn either for local home consumption or for export.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) regulated by the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 247], complemented by customs duty and excise duty applicable to alcoholic beverages withdrawn from bonded warehouses in Vanuatu.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover (compulsory); voluntary registration is permitted below this threshold for ICs expecting to make only zero-rated export supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance regime, e-invoicing API mandate, or digital stamping requirement is currently operational in Vanuatu. Taxpayers must issue sequentially numbered tax invoices in paper or PDF form showing supplier name, VAT identification number, date, description of goods, quantity, and rate. Bonded wine and spirit removals must be supported by customs clearance records in the ASYCUDA environment and the licensed warehouse operator must maintain an excise control ledger; digital fiscal clearance is limited to customs manifest data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under section 11 of the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 247] to goods physically exported from Vanuatu and to prescribed offshore services supplied to non-residents. For bonded wine and spirits, eligibility requires that the goods are removed from a licensed bonded warehouse solely for export, that the IC holds the contract with the foreign buyer, and that export occurs within the statutory 28-day window from removal from bond. Goods supplied by an IC to residents of Vanuatu are ineligible for zero-rating and would be taxable at 13% if permitted under the IC licensing conditions. Input VAT incurred on bonded storage, importation, and freight can be recovered by the IC through periodic VAT returns where the corresponding supply is zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration cleared by Vanuatu Customs and explicitly flagged as export
Original Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing delivery to a destination outside Vanuatu
Bonded warehouse withdrawal order and excise removal certificate showing release of goods from the licensed warehouse
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin (EUR.1 or Form A where preferential treatment is claimed)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 receipt evidencing payment by the foreign buyer
VAT tax invoice printed with the IC's VAT registration number and an unambiguous zero-rated annotation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export substantiation documents must be retained for at least 7 years. Where an IC cannot demonstrate physical export and receipt of foreign currency within the required period, the VCIRC may reassess the supply as taxable at 13%, claw back all input credits previously refunded, and impose interest at 1.5% per month from the date the refund was issued. Civil penalties of up to 50% of the VAT sought to be avoided (minimum VT 50,000) apply for false or incomplete documentation, and fraudulent zero-rating claims are referred for criminal prosecution under the Value Added Tax Act and the Customs Act, carrying fines of up to VT 20,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 10 years. Retrospective assessments may extend over the preceding 5 years in cases involving intentionally misleading export evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vanuatu vatu (VUV) is freely convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Vanuatu has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations; there are no exchange controls, no prior approval requirements for inward or outward remittances, and no restrictions on profit or dividend remittances. All foreign exchange receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts either locally or offshore.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Vanuatu does not impose statutory export proceeds surrender, repatriation, or conversion requirements. Exporters are free to hold trade receipts in VUV or any foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with multi-currency treasury services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Vanuatu Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account for trade license compliance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Vanuatu has no dedicated electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing framework. Offshore digital EMIs without a physical licensed banking presence cannot provide regulated treasury clearing or escrow services in-country. An international company engaged in bonded wine and spirits trade must bank through a licensed domestic commercial bank to maintain statutory audit trails and satisfy trade finance counterparties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Vanuatu's Banks Act and RBV AML/CFT directives require face-to-face verification for corporate directors unless a specific bank-issued remote onboarding waiver is granted. In practice, a physical visit by at least one director and a company secretary is required for initial relationship establishment; remaining principals may be verified through notarized powers of attorney and independent legal certification. Remote opening for high-risk trading classifications is rarely permitted without an already-domiciled local bank reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographical and trade-based money laundering risk associated with bonded alcohol wholesale and cross-border invoicing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed bonded warehouse agreement; VFSC trade licence (ISIC 4632); detailed goods flow description with track-and-trace certificates; registered contract with non-resident distributors; invoice registry with WCO standard data; and retention of title deed under bonding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual volume of high-value wires to low-tax jurisdictions or non-resident intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership register (RBV-compliant); explanatory memorandum on commercial structure; original bills of lading and ocean freight contracts; customs entry declarations (CUSVAD); bank reference letters; and professional tax advisory opinion confirming substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency in turnover versus declared paid-up capital for an international company with no minimum capital requirement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory declarations of source of funds; capital adequacy report prepared by a Vanuatu-licensed accountant; forecast cash flow statement applying to the bonded trade; and supporting warehouse collateral evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed by SWIFT wire to the company's operational VUV or multi-currency account at a licensed Vanuatu commercial bank. For regulatory transparency, the wire must include the corporate name, standard ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g., 'COST' for equity injection or 'TRADE' for working capital), and an accompanying remittance advice referencing the corporate bond and VFSC licence numbers. The RBV maintains no exchange control authorisation step; however, a bank may require a board resolution and signed declaration of beneficial ownership for amounts exceeding VUV 1,000,000 or equivalent foreign currency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Permissible clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and documentary commercial letters of credit (L/C) for larger transactions involving warehouse release against payment. For bonded transfers, the bank will accept inland bonded-transfer instructions subject to a duty-deferred certificate from Vanuatu Customs. Settlement must be under the latest ICC UCP 600 or URC 522 for collections; all outbound packets must include the wine age-serial certificate, warehouse release order, and commercial invoice to satisfy AML transaction monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign exchange contracts up to 12 months (subject to bank credit line)
FX swaps and rollover forwards for trade settlements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore with a licensed international bank (RBV does not restrict offshore hedging, but the economic hedge must be evidenced)
Cross-currency swaps for matched long-term funding of bonded inventory, executed with a counterparty formally authorised under the Financial Dealers Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of International Company Registration and Annual License Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – International Companies Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June each year; companies incorporated after 30 June are carried into the following renewal cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a penalty levied by VFSC; continued non-payment after notice exposes the IC to administrative strike-off, loss of legal capacity, and vesting of assets in VFSC under the International Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Customs Bonded Warehouse Licence for Wine and Spirits Bonded Operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Department – Customs Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application lodged no later than 30 calendar days before the annual licence expiry anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An expired licence suspends duty-suspension and bonded-transfer privileges; continued bonded activity without renewal may result in customs penalties, seizure of excisable goods, recovery of unpaid duties, and licence cancellation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a Vanuatu International Company. Audited financial statements are not required to be filed with VFSC unless the IC holds a licence under a regulated VFSC Act such as insurance, banking, or trust company activities. Ordinary wine and spirits bonded wholesale trade does not trigger a mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act and related financial services regulations require the IC to retain accounting records sufficient to explain transactions and disclose its financial position with reasonable accuracy. There is no mandatory adoption of IFRS or Vanuatu local GAAP for a tax-exempt IC; voluntary financial statements may be prepared under IFRS or an acceptable local accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vanuatu International Company law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing. The registered agent must maintain beneficial ownership records and update the VFSC register promptly upon any change in directors, members, or significant controllers. The annual renewal event is not a shareholding-transfer confirmation point; transfers are recorded in the statutory registers at the time of transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – USD 1,200 per annum for licensed registered agent and registered office services in Vanuatu
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit required; voluntary certified audit typically ranges from USD 2,500 – USD 6,000 per annum for a wholesale trading entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Vanuatu levies no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, payroll tax, or VAT. International Companies are statutorily exempt from income taxation under the International Companies Act and are subject only to annual fees and annual return requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is required. International Companies must file an annual return under Section 104 of the International Companies Act through the registered agent using the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) registered-agent e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed with VFSC within one month after the anniversary of incorporation; late filing is subject to late fees and may trigger strike-off proceedings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate name and International Company registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name and IC number as shown on the certificate of incorporation; use English alphabet characters only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address in Vanuatu of the registered office and registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure a licensed registered agent is engaged; the address must be a real local address and cannot be a post office box alone.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, nationalities, residential addresses, and shareholding details of directors and members.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident natural persons may be listed; provide full legal names and passport details. Beneficial ownership information must be disclosed to the registered agent for VFSC AML compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the registered agent that the company is in compliance with the International Companies Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must sign; non-resident directors cannot substitute for this declaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return attracts monetary late fees imposed by the VFSC. Continuous non-filing leads to administrative strike-off, dissolution, and a reinstatement fee. Knowingly filing false statements may result in personal penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu does not impose dividend withholding tax and has no comprehensive double taxation agreements in force. A tax residency certificate or treaty relief procedure is therefore not applicable for outbound dividends. Non-resident shareholders should apply their domestic foreign tax credit rules privately.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax is 0% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates are not applicable as Vanuatu has no income tax treaties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory transfer pricing documentation threshold exists in Vanuatu in local currency (VUV). Cross-border related-party transactions by International Companies should nevertheless be supported by contemporaneous documentation, including business purpose and arm's-length pricing, to satisfy VFSC substance reviews and anti-money-laundering obligations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu does not maintain a formal Economic Substance Regulations regime for International Companies. However, a licensed bonded trade business in wine and spirits must demonstrate genuine local substance, including physical storage premises, local licence possession, and appointed licensed directors/agents, to meet VFSC licensing and AML/CFT standards.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Vanuatu International Company to conceal a taxable permanent establishment or trading activities carried on in a foreign jurisdiction, or submitting false declarations to VFSC that the entity is engaged only in exempt activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative strike-off and deregistration by VFSC; disqualification of the registered agent; substantial monetary fines under the International Companies Act for false statements; forfeiture of bonds or guarantees associated with the wine/spirits licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid fines and third-party losses. Knowingly making false declarations can lead to personal travel bans and imprisonment for related fraud offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company without a physical presence, local registered office, licensed warehouse, or substance, while processing bonded transfers of wine and spirits solely as a pass-through finance vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the International Company status, striking off the corporate registry, revocation of the bonded warehouse licence, freezing of bank accounts, and monetary penalties for breach of the International Companies Act and licensing conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal civil liability for company debts where the company is adjudged a sham. Travel bans and director disqualification may be ordered, and imprisonment applies to those who operate a shell company to facilitate fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform customer due diligence on alcohol purchasers; accepting SWIFT wire transfers from undisclosed beneficial owners; executing bonded transfers to another jurisdiction without customs approval; concealing the true value of Scotch or Bordeaux wine shipments to evade excise duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: License suspension or revocation under the Customs Act and VFSC licensing rules; asset forfeiture and fines under the Vanuatu AML/CFT framework; criminal prosecution for money laundering and customs fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be criminally prosecuted; imprisonment up to 10 years for money-laundering offences; personal fines; prohibition from holding any directorship or licensed position in Vanuatu; potential international travel restrictions while proceedings are pending.
